CYM-bounty-filing-unauthenticated.title: Filing a bug report passes authorization with no credential: hunter attribution rests on an unauthenticated form field
CYM-bounty-filing-unauthenticated.note: POST /api/v1/bounty/reports with an empty body returns a byte-identical validation error with no key and with a TRUSTED key. No authorization check runs before validation. If that holds for a populated body, hunter_name is a field any caller sets freely and reward attribution is unauthenticated. SCOPE: an empty body shows only that auth does not run FIRST. It does not show a fully-populated anonymous POST is accepted -- testing that would create a real record in their tracker, so it is asked, not done. Verified after probing that the tracker total was unchanged at 23.

CYM-llms_agent_count_self_consistent.title: Does llms.txt quote the same agent count in all of its own sentences?
CYM-llms_agent_count_self_consistent.note: A document that contradicts itself is worse than two documents that disagree, because the reader has no way to pick. Added after report #52 updated one occurrence of the count and left another behind.

CYM-mcp_tool_names_documented_exist.title: Does every tool name llms.txt documents exist on the server?
CYM-mcp_tool_names_documented_exist.note: Subset, not set_equal. llms.txt is not obliged to list every tool -- it is obliged not to name one that does not exist. The earlier set_equal form would now fail simply because the document lists fewer than the server serves, which is correct behaviour.

CYM-own-reports-unverified.title: 11 reports filed under our hunter name were closed by the platform and have never been re-verified by us
CYM-own-reports-unverified.note: The resolution notes are specific -- they name files, line numbers and commit hashes. That is better than most vendors provide and it is worth crediting. It is still a claim: the commits are not inspectable from here, validated_at is null, and our own records still list these as open with last_regression_run: null. Correct state is FIX_CLAIMED, not fixed. Note also that all six are UI defects in arena.js, outside this project's API/MCP scope -- re-verifying them needs the browser suite, not this one.

CYM-skills_subset.title: Is agent-skills.json the actionable subset of agent-card.json, as stated?
CYM-skills_subset.note: Their resolution on #51 states agent-card.json is the full discovery card and agent-skills.json the endpoint-actionable subset. That is a testable model and the right one, so this checks the claim they actually made rather than demanding the two files be identical -- which they explained, correctly, that they should not be.

CYM-tracker-closure-rate.title: All 15 reports in the public bounty tracker read 'fixed', and validated_at is null on every one
CYM-tracker-closure-rate.note: A queue with a 100% closure rate and no open, triaged, disputed or wont_fix item is not a queue -- it is either a filtered view or a tracker that does not retain unresolved items. The schema HAS validated_at, triaged_at and severity_confirmed fields; none is populated on any record. SCOPE: this says nothing about whether the underlying fixes are real. It says the tracker records no evidence that anyone checked.

CYM-documented-404.title: 26 endpoints the platform documents return 404
CYM-documented-404.note: This does not establish which of two things is true. Either the endpoints were removed and the documents are stale, or the documents are aspirational and these were never built. An agent following llms.txt cannot tell the difference, and neither can we -- the platform has to say which.
